jobs.description:
1. Identificación del Cargo

Título del cargo: Carrier Relations and Routing

Ubicación: Colombia (Hibrido)

Alcance geográfico: Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica
Tipo de relación: Gestión de relaciones y optimización de enrutamiento (routing) con operadoras (carriers) de telecomunicaciones
2. Propósito del Cargo
El Carrier Agent es responsable de establecer, desarrollar y mantener relaciones comerciales sólidas y duraderas con operadoras de telecomunicaciones en Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica, así como de monitorear y contribuir a la optimización del enrutamiento (routing) del tráfico con dichas operadoras. Este cargo es clave para asegurar acuerdos beneficiosos, coordinar operaciones conjuntas, dar seguimiento a la calidad y el costo de las rutas, y representar a la empresa como un socio confiable y cercano ante las operadoras, todo esto gestionado de forma remota pero con un nivel de cercanía y calidez propio de una relación presencial.
3. Responsabilidades Principales
• Construir y mantener relaciones comerciales cercanas y de confianza con operadoras de telecomunicaciones en Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica
• Actuar como punto de contacto principal entre la empresa y las operadoras, gestionando la comunicación de manera fluida, cordial y profesional.
• Negociar términos comerciales, tarifas y acuerdos de interconexión que beneficien a ambas partes.
• Monitorear el desempeño de las relaciones con cada operadora, identificando oportunidades de mejora o expansión del negocio.
• Monitorear indicadores técnicos de las rutas de tráfico (SMS y/o voz) por operadora, como tasa de entrega, latencia y calidad, en coordinación con los equipos técnicos y de producto.
• Contribuir a la optimización de rutas (Least Cost Routing) evaluando costo, calidad y capacidad de cada operadora.
• Detectar y escalar oportunamente problemas de enrutamiento (caídas de entrega, filtrado, rutas grises) ante las operadoras y las áreas internas correspondientes.
• Coordinar reuniones virtuales periódicas con las operadoras para fortalecer el vínculo y dar seguimiento a compromisos pendientes.
• Resolver de manera proactiva y diplomática cualquier inconveniente o fricción que surja en la relación comercial.
• Identificar nuevas oportunidades de negocio y potenciales operadoras con las cuales establecer alianzas.
• Reportar periódicamente a la gerencia sobre el estado de las relaciones, negociaciones en curso y resultados obtenidos.
• Representar a la empresa en eventos, llamadas y espacios de networking del sector, incluso de forma virtual.
4. Perfil del Candidato
Habilidades interpersonales (esenciales para este cargo)
• Carisma natural y facilidad para generar empatía y confianza desde el primer contacto.
• Sociabilidad genuina: disfruta conectar con personas de distintas culturas, países y estilos de trabajo.
• Excelentes habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita, tanto en español como, idealmente, en inglés.
• Capacidad comprobada para construir relaciones comerciales fuertes y de largo plazo, incluso a distancia.
• Habilidad para leer el contexto cultural y adaptar su estilo de comunicación según el interlocutor (Colombia, Venezuela, México, Centroamérica).
• Actitud positiva, proactiva y orientada al servicio, incluso bajo presión o en negociaciones complejas.
Formación y experiencia
• Formación en Telecomunicaciones, Negocios Internacionales, Administración, Relaciones Comerciales o áreas afines.
• Experiencia previa en roles de account management, ventas B2B, relaciones con carriers o gestión comercial, preferiblemente en el sector telco.
• Conocimiento del mercado de telecomunicaciones en Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica (deseable).
• Experiencia trabajando de forma remota y gestionando relaciones interculturales.
Competencias técnicas
• Manejo de herramientas de videoconferencia, CRM, Google Workspace, Slack y Hubspot (deseable).
• Conocimiento de conceptos de enrutamiento de tráfico de telecomunicaciones (Least Cost Routing, calidad de ruta, tasa de entrega) (deseable, se puede entrenar).
• Manejo de herramientas o plataformas de monitoreo de tráfico y reporting de KPIs (deseable).
• Capacidad de análisis de tráfico, tarifas, acuerdos de interconexión e indicadores de calidad de ruta (deseable, se puede entrenar).
• Organización y disciplina para el trabajo remoto autónomo.
5. Condiciones del Cargo
• Modalidad: 100% remoto, con base en Colombia.
• Disponibilidad para reuniones en distintos horarios según la contraparte (Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica).
• Disponibilidad para viajar ocasionalmente si la empresa lo requiere (según necesidad del negocio).
6. Perfil Ideal en Una Frase
Buscamos una persona carismática, sociable y con habilidades naturales para conectar y generar confianza, capaz de convertir cada interacción con una operadora en el inicio de una relación comercial sólida y duradera, sin importar la distancia.

 

JOB DESCRIPTION

Carrier Relations and Routing — Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America (Remote)

1. Position Identification

Job title: Carrier Relations and Routing

Location: Colombia (Hybrid position)

Geographic scope: Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America
Type of relationship: Management of relationships and routing optimization with telecommunications operators (carriers)
Work arrangement: Remote work with constant, direct interaction with counterparts across the region

2. Purpose of the Position

The Carrier Agent is responsible for establishing, developing and maintaining strong, long-lasting commercial relationships with telecommunications operators in Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America, as well as monitoring and contributing to the optimization of traffic routing with those operators. This position is key to securing mutually beneficial agreements, coordinating joint operations, tracking route quality and cost, and representing the company as a trusted, close partner before the operators — all managed remotely, but with the same closeness and warmth as an in-person relationship.

3. Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain close, trust-based commercial relationships with telecommunications operators in Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America.
    • Act as the main point of contact between the company and the operators, managing communication in a smooth, cordial and professional manner.
    • Negotiate commercial terms, rates and interconnection agreements that benefit both parties.
    • Monitor the performance of the relationship with each operator, identifying opportunities to improve or expand the business.
    • Monitor technical route performance indicators (SMS and/or voice) per operator, such as delivery rate, latency and quality, in coordination with technical and product teams.
    • Contribute to route optimization (Least Cost Routing) by evaluating cost, quality and capacity of each operator.
    • Proactively detect and escalate routing issues (delivery drops, filtering, grey routes) to operators and the relevant internal teams.
    • Coordinate regular virtual meetings with the operators to strengthen the relationship and follow up on outstanding commitments.
    • Proactively and diplomatically resolve any issue or friction that arises in the commercial relationship.
    • Identify new business opportunities and potential operators with which to establish partnerships.
    • Report regularly to management on the status of relationships, ongoing negotiations and results achieved.
    • Represent the company at industry events, calls and networking spaces, including virtually.

4. Candidate Profile

Interpersonal skills (essential for this position)
• Natural charisma and an ease for building empathy and trust from the very first contact.
• Genuine sociability: enjoys connecting with people from different cultures, countries and working styles.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills, in Spanish and, ideally, in English.
• Proven ability to build strong, long-term commercial relationships, even remotely.
• Ability to read the cultural context and adapt communication style to each counterpart (Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico, Central America).
• Positive, proactive and service-oriented attitude, even under pressure or in complex negotiations.

Education and experience

  • Education in Telecommunications, International Business, Business Administration, Commercial Relations or related fields.
    • Previous experience in account management, B2B sales, carrier relations or commercial management roles, preferably in the telco sector.
    • Knowledge of the telecommunications market in Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America (desirable).
    • Experience working remotely and managing cross-cultural relationships.
    Technical skills
    • Proficiency with videoconferencing tools, CRM, Google Workspace, Slack and HubSpot (desirable).
    • Familiarity with telecom traffic routing concepts (Least Cost Routing, route quality, delivery rate) (desirable; can be trained).
    • Proficiency with traffic monitoring tools or KPI reporting platforms (desirable).
    • Ability to analyze traffic, rates, interconnection agreements and route quality indicators (desirable; can be trained).
    • Organization and discipline for autonomous remote work.

5. Position Conditions

  • Work arrangement: hybrid, based in Colombia.
    • Availability for meetings at different times depending on the counterpart (Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico, Central America).
    • Availability to travel occasionally if required by the company (based on business needs).

6. Ideal Profile in One Sentence

We are looking for a charismatic, sociable person with a natural ability to connect and build trust — someone able to turn every interaction with an operator into the beginning of a strong, lasting commercial relationship, no matter the distance.

Location

This position will be located in Colombia. You will get to experience a company that believes in small teams for maximum impact; seeks well-rounded talent to ensure a full perspective on our customers’ experience, understands that this is a marathon, not a sprint; that continuously and purposefully builds an inclusive culture where everyone is able to do and be the best version of themselves.

About Us

Since 2001, Messangi has been connecting companies to their customers on billions of devices around the world. Our versatile and reliable platforms have been built in-house by some of the top engineers in the business. To power our operations, we have world-class teams in 7 countries willing to go the extra mile to meet our customers’ needs. Today, top mobile operators, global banks, and retailers rely on Messangi to solve their customer communication and engagement

Senior Marketing Manager

Remote, US

About Nametag
Nametag is building the future of secure digital identity. Our mission is to protect every human identity to restore trust in the AI era. We bring workforce-grade identity verification into the enterprise to verify the human behind accounts and critical actions. Today, global enterprises use Nametag across their workforce to prevent social engineering and deepfake impersonation attacks.

The Role

Nametag is hiring a Senior Marketing Manager to be one of the primary hands on our content engine; the person who can take a product update, a customer story, or an industry trend and turn it into a blog post, an email, a one-pager, and a social thread. This role leans content: you should be, first and foremost, an excellent writer who's comfortable in a technical B2B space. It's also a generalist role where you'll move across channels and formats rather than owning one lane, which suits someone who wants breadth over deep specialization in any single channel.

Role Overview

As Senior Marketing Manager, you will own a meaningful share of Nametag's day-to-day content output: blog posts, email newsletters, social copy, website updates, sales one-pagers, and event collateral. You'll work closely with Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, Design, Sales, Customer Success, and Channel Partnerships to keep everything on-voice and moving, and you'll often be the person turning someone else's raw material into something customers, prospects, and partners actually read.

What you’ll do

  1. Content Creation & Editorial Ownership
  • Write and edit the majority of Nametag's recurring content: blog posts, thought-leadership articles, email newsletters, and website copy updates.
  • Maintain a consistent voice and terminology across everything you touch, using Nametag's messaging and style guide as the working standard.
  • Turn technical product detail into copy a security, IT, or HR buyer will want to read, without losing accuracy along the way.
  1. Sales & Customer-Facing Collateral
  • Write and refresh customer-facing collateral: one-pagers, solution briefs, and customer stories.
  • Turn customer conversations and Customer Success input into concrete proof points and case studies.
  • Keep collateral current as messaging and product details change, rather than letting outdated one-pagers keep circulating.
  1. Multi-Channel Campaign Support
  • Write copy supporting Growth Marketing's campaigns across email, social, paid, and landing pages.
  • Adapt a single core message across formats and channels so campaigns feel coordinated rather than assembled from parts.
  • Support A/B testing of messaging and creative with fresh copy variants.
  1. Event & Field Marketing Content
  • Produce content supporting Nametag's conference presence and field events: talk-track material, dinner and panel briefs, and pre- and post-event follow-up content.
  • Partner with Channel Partnerships on content for partner-facing events and co-marketing moments.
  1. Editorial Calendar & Cross-Functional Coordination
  • Own and maintain the marketing content calendar, coordinating inputs from Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, Design, and Sales so nothing ships late, off-voice, or duplicated.
  • Flag gaps and inconsistencies in existing content and messaging, and drive them to resolution rather than letting them sit.
  1. Performance & Iteration
  • Track content performance: engagement, email metrics, content-influenced pipeline, in partnership with Growth Marketing, and use it to prioritize what to write next.

What You Bring

We encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply, even if you don't meet every listed qualification. You'll thrive in this role if you bring most of the following:

  • ~8 years in B2B marketing, with some of that time in a content-heavy role: content marketing, editorial, communications, or a marketing generalist role centered on writing.
  • Genuine comfort as a generalist. Someone who'd rather move across several channels well than own one channel deeply.

jobs.excerpt: About Riot Platforms Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure.
jobs.description:
About Riot Platforms

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. Riot’s mission is to empower the future of digital infrastructure by positively impacting the sectors, networks, and communities that we touch. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Who we are

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure.

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About the role

The Director, Governance owns the foundational infrastructure every other GRC pillar depends on. Without a policy library, Compliance has nothing to test. Without regulatory horizon scanning, risk finds Riot before Riot finds risk. Without a contracts management program, vendor and third-party risk runs unchecked. Governance is the bedrock of this program — and this role builds it from near zero in Year 1.

This pillar is intentionally scoped to govern, not to test or audit. Governance owns the full lifecycle of policies and standards: drafting, approval routing, versioning, publication, and attestation tracking. Governance owns the ISO 27001:2022 documentation framework — all mandatory policy and procedure documents required for certification. Governance owns the regulatory radar, the Contracts Management program (in co-ownership with Legal), and the Third-Party Risk Management program (in partnership with Procurement).

You will report to the Senior Director, GRC and maintain a co-ownership relationship with the Chief Legal Officer on Contracts Management, where Legal holds final sign-off authority at every material decision gate. In critical operations, you will engage mining site and data center leadership to ensure site-level operational policies, physical security standards, and environmental procedures are captured within the enterprise governance framework.

What you'll do

  • Build and own the ISO 27001:2022 documentation framework: identify and produce all mandatory policies, procedures, and records required for certification, map them to Annex A controls, and drive adoption through executive sponsorship and attestation programs — this is the Year 1 priority with a contractually fixed delivery timeline.
  • Build and operate the Riot policy and standards library from near-zero baseline: establish the governance model (drafting, review routing, approval gates, versioning, renewal cadences), and extend scope beyond ISO 27001 to cover SOC 2, SOX, and enterprise policy requirements.
  • Own the regulatory horizon scanning program: monitor developments across critical infrastructure, digital assets, data privacy, and financial services; translate regulatory signals into GRC program actions; and deliver regular briefings to the Sr. Director and executive leadership.
  • Stand up the Contracts Management program in co-ownership with Legal: design the intake-to-repository workflow, establish GRC risk flagging criteria (data processing, liability, security, regulatory), and implement the Legal sign-off gate — Legal approves, GRC operates.
  • Own the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) and vendor risk program: build the vendor tiering model, define due diligence requirements by tier, partner with Procurement on intake integration, and establish ongoing monitoring cadences for critical and colocation vendors.
  • Manage the GRC framework lifecycle: maintain Riot's mapping of policies and controls to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, and applicable regulatory frameworks — keeping the library current as the regulatory and audit environment evolves.
  • Engage critical operations to ensure site-level operational policies, physical security standards, and environmental procedures are captured within the governance framework and aligned to enterprise GRC standards.

What you'll bring

  • 8–12+ years of progressive GRC, policy management, regulatory affairs, or governance program experience at a publicly traded or highly regulated company.
  • ISO 27001 Lead Implementer certification — required. The Director, Governance is the primary owner of ISO 27001:2022 policy and documentation implementation. Riot has an active, contractually required certification obligation; this credential is a baseline requirement, not a differentiator.
  • Demonstrated experience building a policy library from a minimal baseline — governance model design, framework mapping, attestation program rollout, and cross-functional adoption.
  • Experience standing up or operating a Contracts Management program with Legal co-ownership — contract risk review, DPA requirements, and GRC-Legal governance models.
  • Working knowledge of TPRM frameworks and vendor risk program design — tiering models, due diligence questionnaires, and ongoing monitoring processes.
  • Proven regulatory horizon scanning capability across critical infrastructure, digital assets, and data privacy (CISA, FinCEN, state privacy laws, DORA, NIS2 familiarity).
  • Experience mapping a policy library to multiple frameworks simultaneously (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF) to support a unified audit and control program.
  • Strong cross-functional communication and influence: ability to drive policy adoption and contracts governance across Legal, Procurement, HR, and Operations without direct authority.
  • Preferred: CISM, CGEIT, CRISC, or CIPP/US certification; experience in critical infrastructure, energy, data center, or digital asset environments.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: Base range (commensurate with experience) + bonus + sign-on equity grant.
  • Long-Term Growth: Eligible to participate in Riot’s equity incentive programs and share in the success you help build.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Incudes a generous company match.
  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans.
  • Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work.

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

We're looking for a Senior Vice President, Strategy to lead and evolve our strategy practice across the Americas. Practice Leadership

If you do not meet all the listed qualifications or have gaps in your experience, we still encourage you to apply. At Valtech, we recognize that talent comes in many forms, and we value diverse perspectives and a willingness to learn.

The benefits

jobs.description:
POS-33475

Senior Business Systems Analyst, Partner Systems & Automation

About the Team

HubSpot's Partner Systems & Automation team builds the systems, automations, and integrations that power HubSpot's partner ecosystem — one of the most strategically important parts of the business, representing a significant share of HubSpot revenue. We work across HubSpot's internal CRM portals, Workato, ServiceNow, Snowflake, and a range of third-party systems, and we are actively expanding our use of AI-assisted workflows to move faster from problem identification to working solutions.

We identify problems, design solutions, build them, ship them, and own them. Our BSAs sit at the boundary between business operations and technical execution — close enough to the business to understand what matters, and technical enough to build it. We are looking for a Senior BSA who thinks like a builder, operates like an engineer, and communicates like a business partner.

In This Role, You'll Get To

  • Take ownership of complex, cross-functional automation and systems work across HubSpot's Solutions Partner program — one of the most mature and technically demanding parts of our partner ecosystem
  • Identify inefficiencies and root causes across partner operations workflows, then design, build, test, and ship solutions
  • Build and maintain integrations, automations, and data pipelines using Workato and HubSpot CRM, with SQL and REST APIs as standard tools of the trade
  • Prototype AI-assisted workflows and automation agents, bringing them from idea to working implementation and iterating based on real usage data
  • Scope work rigorously — define the problem, quantify the impact, propose the right-sized solution, and know when to prototype before committing to a full build
  • Partner with stakeholders across Partner Operations, Partner Product, Engineering, Finance, and Analytics to translate business problems into technical solutions
  • Push back constructively when a request does not justify the investment, and help stakeholders understand why
  • Operate across multiple partner program domains over time — Solutions Partners is your primary home, but this team is deliberately moving toward cross-domain capability and you will be part of that shift
  • Contribute to the team's technical standards and share what you learn, so useful discoveries by one person become capabilities for everyone

We Are Looking For Someone With

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience in a role where you built and shipped production systems — business systems analyst, automation engineer, internal tools engineer, or similarly technical operations role
  • Technical fluency across the systems stack — SQL, REST APIs, Python, and JSON are standard tools for you; you use them to understand, diagnose, and extend systems
  • Hands-on experience with iPaaS tools (Workato, Zapier, Boomi, or similar) — building and maintaining multi-step automations and integrations across complex systems
  • Comfort with engineering hygiene for production systems — version control, incremental rollouts, and basic testing practices that make what you build safe to operate and easy for others to maintain.
  • Either shipped an AI-assisted feature or automation that real users used, or have a strong production track record and genuine interest in applying AI to operational workflows
  • Comfort working in ambiguous environments where the right problem is not always the stated problem — you ask the questions that reframe the work before you start building
  • Experience working across multiple stakeholder groups with different incentives and priorities, and the ability to align people without formal authority
  • Strong written and verbal communication — you can explain a complex system to a non-technical audience and a complex business problem to an engineer
  • A sense of ownership that extends past delivery — you define expected outcomes before you build, check them after you ship, and treat the systems you own as your ongoing responsibility

Pay & Benefits

The cash compensation below includes base salary, on-target commission for employees in eligible roles, and annual bonus targets under HubSpot’s bonus plan for eligible roles. In addition to cash compensation, some roles are eligible to participate in HubSpot’s equity plan to receive restricted stock units (RSUs). Individual compensation packages are determined using objective, role-related criteria, which may include skills, experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

This resource will help guide how we recommend thinking about the range you see.

Benefits are also an important piece of your total compensation package. Explore the benefits and perks HubSpot offers to help employees grow better.

At HubSpot, fair compensation practices aren’t just about checking off the box for legal compliance. It’s about living out our value of transparency with our employees, candidates, and community.

Annual Cash Compensation Range:
€63.400—€87.150 EUR

At HubSpot, we value both flexibility and connection. Whether you’re a Remote employee or work from the Office, we want you to start your journey here by building strong connections with your team and peers. If you are joining our Engineering team, you will be required to attend a regional HubSpot office for in-person onboarding. If you join our broader Product team, you’ll also attend other in-person events, such as your Product Group Summit and other gatherings, to continue building on those connections.

If you require an accommodation due to travel limitations or other reasons, please inform your recruiter during the hiring process. We are committed to supporting candidates who may need alternative arrangements

About HubSpot

HubSpot (NYSE: HUBS) is an AI-powered customer platform with all the software, integrations, and resources customers need to connect marketing, sales, and service. HubSpot's connected platform enables businesses to grow faster by focusing on what matters most: customers.

At HubSpot, bold is our baseline. Our employees around the globe move fast, stay customer-obsessed, and win together. Our culture is grounded in four commitments: Solve for the Customer, Be Bold, Learn Fast, Align, Adapt & Go!, and Deliver with HEART. These commitments shape how we work, lead, and grow.

We’re building a company where people can do their best work. We focus on brilliant work, not badge swipes. By combining clarity, ownership, and trust, we create space for big thinking and meaningful progress. And we know that when our employees grow, our customers do too.

Recognized globally for our award-winning culture by Comparably, Glassdoor, Fortune, and more, HubSpot is headquartered in Cambridge, MA, with employees and offices around the world.

jobs.description:
INNERGY is the platform for the joinery industry — cloud ERP, CAD/CAM and shop-drawings services for the joinery and cabinetry manufacturers who build the casework, wall panels and fixtures inside the buildings you use every day. We’re specialists, not generalists: we replace the QuickBooks, Excel, AutoCAD and email stack most shops run on. Today that’s 520+ ERP customers and 1,800+ CAD/CAM customers, with ~25% of those within the Oceania region.

The Regional Director, Oceania role is accountable for owning the strategy, the customers, and the commercial results in the region.

This is a matrix role. The Sales, Account Management, Marketing, Customer Success and Support people serving Oceania report solid-line to their global functional leaders and dotted-line to you. You set the regional agenda and deliver it through influence and credibility rather than the org chart.

Responsibilities

Commercial

  • Own the Oceania number — new business, expansion and retention

  • Set regional strategy, the operating plan and segment focus; decide which parts of the AU/NZ joinery market we serve and which we don’t

  • Own the regional budget and deliver a forecast leadership can plan against

  • Own regional contribution margin — revenue, direct costs and the local cost base

Operational

  • Build and run the regional operating rhythm: pipeline reviews, account planning, escalation handling, and the cadence that keeps four functions aligned

  • In partnership with Sales Leadership, drive pipeline health, forecast accuracy and deal strategy on the deals that matter

  • Drive time-to-value, adoption, renewal and support quality for every AU/NZ customer

  • Solve the time zone gap between the regional customer base and US-based support

People and Influence

  • Shape hiring profiles, participate in the recruiting, interviewing, and hiring of regional teammates, and contribute to performance conversations alongside functional managers

  • Earn the trust and cooperation of global functional leaders; escalate cleanly when alignment fails

  • Build what it means to work at INNERGY in this market

Market and Company

  • Represent INNERGY in-region: Education, associations, industry events, partnerships and the local narrative

  • Serve as Oceania’s voice into product and leadership on what’s different here and what we need to win

  • Operational fluency in joinery, manufacturing, construction tech or building products — credible with shop owners on margins, throughput and why the estimate was wrong

  • Experience running a complex B2B software business: long cycles, multiple stakeholders, implementation-heavy products

  • Prior ownership of a regional business or P&L, not just a quota

  • Demonstrated results delivered through a matrix — accountable for outcomes owned by people who didn’t report to you, with a specific example they can walk through

  • Exposure to both sales and post-sale functions

  • Commercial judgment to decline bad-fit business and explain why

  • Based in AEST/AEDT or NZST; legal right to work in Australia or New Zealand

  • Willing to travel ~40% in-region plus 1–2 US trips per year

  • Existing network in AU/NZ joinery, construction or manufacturing

  • Experience representing a region for an offshore-headquartered company

Accessibility & Work Environment

INNERGY is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible work environment. We support reasonable workplace adjustments for individuals with disability in accordance with applicable Australian laws. If you require adjustments during the recruitment process or in your role, please let us know.

This role is primarily computer-based and may involve extended screen time and regular communication through digital channels. Work may be performed in a remote or office-based environment, depending on role and location. INNERGY is committed to supporting employee wellbeing, flexibility, and a safe working environment across all regions.

INNERGY is transforming the woodworking industry with purpose built, cloud based ERP software designed exclusively for custom manufacturers. Our platform helps businesses operate smarter, faster, and more efficiently while seamlessly connecting design, production, and delivery for teams creating architectural millwork, cabinetry, and casework.

What truly sets INNERGY apart is our people. Founded in 2016, we are a globally distributed team of 200 plus professionals united by deep software expertise and a shared passion for solving meaningful, real world problems. We value collaboration, creativity, and ownership, and we are intentional about building not only powerful products, but also a culture where people feel supported, heard, and inspired to do their best work.

With strong momentum and the recent acquisition of Microvellum, a trusted leader in design to manufacturing solutions for the woodworking industry, INNERGY is entering an exciting new phase of growth. This combination expands our capabilities, deepens our industry impact, and accelerates our vision of delivering a truly connected, end to end platform for custom manufacturers.

As we scale thoughtfully and bring together top talent and new perspectives, this is a unique opportunity to join a company where your work will have visible impact, your ideas will help shape decisions, and your contributions will play a meaningful role in defining the future of a fast evolving product, team, and industry.

jobs.description:
About Sundays for Dogs

Sundays for Dogs is a founder-led, direct-to-consumer brand reimagining pet food so dog owners can spend more quality time with their dogs — now and later. We make human-grade, air-dried food that supports long, healthy lives, and we build our company around shared core values that guide how we work and how we treat each other.

We’re headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, with a primarily remote team of ~50 full-time employees across the U.S. While we work distributed day to day, we come together in person on a quarterly basis because relationships matter. Our business today is 100% DTC, with our subscription model at the core of how we serve customers — and we’re building to scale with intention. We’re just getting started...

About your team and position:

The Operations team at Sundays for Dogs spans supply chain, fulfillment, quality, and is responsible for getting a premium, perishable product into customers' hands reliably as we scale from roughly $110M toward $250M. We run on an EOS/L10 operating cadence, which means clear ownership, weekly accountability, and a bias toward solving root causes over patching symptoms. We're in the middle of standing up a formal S&OP process and rebuilding our co-manufacturing network, so there's real ground to break in this role rather than a process to simply maintain.

The Sr. Planner will own the S&OP process end to end: demand planning, supply planning, and the monthly cycle that brings them together into one forecast the business can trust. You'll build the demand forecast, translate it into supply and purchasing plans across our co-manufacturing network, and own the inventory and service level outcomes that follow. This is a highly analytical, highly cross-functional role. You'll be the person who can say with confidence what we expect to sell, what we need to make, and what that means for inventory and cash.

The Sr. Planner reports to the Sr. Director, Supply Chain. No direct reports today, with room to grow the team as the S&OP process matures. You'll work closely with Purchasing and Logistics on execution, with Finance on inventory and cash implications, with R&D and Quality on new recipe launches and co-manufacturing transitions, and Marketing on demand model inputs and levers.

Your day-to-day:

  • Own the monthly S&OP cycle end to end, building the demand forecast, reconciling it with supply capacity, and driving the meeting where the business aligns on one number.
  • Build and maintain the demand forecast by SKU and channel, incorporating promotional activity, subscription trends, and new product launches.
  • Translate the demand forecast into a supply and purchasing plan across our co-manufacturing network, flagging capacity constraints before they become stockouts.
  • Own inventory targets and turns, balancing service level against working capital so we're neither out of stock nor overstocked.
  • Build the reporting that gives the business a clear, trusted view of forecast accuracy, inventory health, and supply risk.
  • Partner with Purchasing and Logistics to convert the supply plan into purchase orders and inbound schedules that actually land on time.
  • Flag and help resolve OOS risk early, working with Marketing, Fulfillment and Customer Care so the business isn't surprised by a stockout.

What success looks like:

First 30 days: Full visibility into current demand and supply data, forecast history, and open OOS risks, with a documented view of how planning works today across every SKU and facility.

First 90 days: A monthly S&OP cycle running on a fixed cadence with a documented process, feeding a single forecast that Purchasing, Marketing, Finance, and Supply Chain leadership all plan against.

Ongoing Metrics: Forecast accuracy, fill rate, and inventory turns tracked and reported on a consistent schedule, with OOS incidents caught and flagged before they hit the customer.

30/60/90 Plan: The scorecard (metrics of performance) and the 30/60/90 day plan for the Sr Planner role is met.

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • You have 5+ years of experience in demand planning, supply planning, or S&OP, ideally in a food, CPG, or DTC subscription business.
  • You have proven experience building or running an S&OP process, not just participating in one someone else designed.
  • You have strong Excel or modeling skills and are comfortable building your own forecasts rather than relying on someone else's output.
  • You have experience planning across a multi-facility or co-manufacturing network, including navigating capacity constraints and lead times.
  • You have the ability to work cross-functionally and hold your ground on the numbers when priorities compete.
  • You have a track record of catching risk early and communicating it clearly, rather than letting it surface as a surprise.
  • You have the ability to operate with real autonomy in a fast-growing environment where you're building process as you go.

jobs.description:
About Lively

Lively set out to raise the bar on benefit solutions, because we believe no one should have to sacrifice personal wellness for financial wellness. While traditional benefits focus more on transactions and less on the humans using them, Lively harnesses user-centric design and innovative technology to deliver an effortless experience for employers and account holders alike. Our modern HSA is consistently top-rated, and we have since expanded our offerings to provide a full suite of other benefits and services for companies, consumers, and financial institutions.

Lively is a remote-first company, headquartered in San Francisco with employees across the US. Come join us and help make getting the value out of your benefits as simple as it should be.

THE ROLE

Lively is hiring a Senior Product Manager to own how data moves between our platform and the systems our customers and partners rely on — payroll and HR platforms, benefits administration systems, carriers, and third-party administrators. You will own enrollment and eligibility data, file-based and API-based exchange, and the integration roadmap that connects Lively to its ecosystem.

You will also own the AI agent experiences that sit on top of that data layer, with a focus on onboarding and validation: agents that help customers and partners get their data into Lively correctly the first time, interpret what arrives, surface problems in plain language, and propose corrections. Integration work at Lively is increasingly AI-assisted, and this role decides where that assistance belongs and where human review stays mandatory.

Alongside this, you will shape Lively's forward data integration strategy: how our connectivity model evolves as the ecosystem moves toward real-time exchange, where we invest in building versus partnering, and how we make each additional integration cheaper and faster than the last.

This is a technically grounded product role. You will work closely with engineering on system behavior, data design, and agent behavior, and you will be the person partners and internal teams come to when they need to understand how the data actually flows. You will own large initiatives end-to-end and operate as the primary subject matter expert for your areas.

Please note: As a majority of our engineering team sits in Pacific time, candidate preference will be given to those in the Pacific and Mountain timezones.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Responsibilities are listed in order of anticipated time investment:

  • Integration Ownership — Own the data exchanged between Lively and its partners: what moves, in what form, on what cadence, and what happens when something goes wrong. Define the contracts that both sides build against.
  • AI-Assisted Data Onboarding & Validation — Own the AI agent experiences that accelerate getting partner and customer data into Lively: interpreting unfamiliar file structures, mapping fields, catching errors before they propagate, explaining what went wrong in language a non-technical administrator can act on, and recommending fixes. Define where the agent acts, where it advises, and where a human must approve.
  • Enrollment & Eligibility Data — Own the enrollment data lifecycle end to end, including how changes, corrections, and exceptions are handled, and how Lively proves its records match the partner's.
  • Reliability, Data Quality & Scale — Own the non-functional requirements of Lively's data integration platform: throughput, latency, availability, recovery, and the guarantee that data is never silently lost or partially applied. Define how failures are detected, communicated, and resolved. Plan capacity for the benefits industry's seasonal enrollment peaks and for growth in partner and record volume. Set the accuracy bar AI-assisted validation must clear before production use.
  • Integration Strategy — Set the multi-year direction for how Lively connects to its ecosystem: the target architecture, the migration path from today's model, the role AI plays in reducing integration effort, and the build/buy/partner decisions that get us there.
  • Requirements & Discovery — Translate partner needs, customer commitments, and regulatory constraints into clear, complete requirements — including the edge cases and failure paths, not only the intended flow.
  • Partner & Implementation Enablement — Support the technical onboarding of new partners from specification through go-live, and reduce the time and effort each new connection takes.
  • Stakeholder Stewardship — Act as the primary SME for your areas, fielding questions from implementation, customer success, sales, and leadership. Communicate vision, roadmap, and progress to internal and external audiences.
  • Roadmap Ownership — Sequence complex, multi-quarter integration work into delivery milestones, balancing customer commitments, partner dependencies, and platform health.
  • Performance Tracking — Define and monitor the metrics that describe integration health, onboarding effort, and AI agent accuracy, and use them to direct investment.
  • AI Fluency in Practice — Use AI tooling in your own product work — research, specification, data analysis, prototyping — and raise the bar for how the product organization does the same.
  • Market Awareness — Track how the benefits, payroll, and data-interoperability landscape is evolving, including where AI is changing what integration work costs, and identify partnership and standardization opportunities.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time owning integrations, data exchange, or platform APIs as a primary product surface
  • Experience owning the exchange of structured business data between organizations — whether by file, API, or both — including the formats, cadence, and correctness guarantees each side depends on
  • Demonstrated ownership of API products, including how they are designed, documented, evolved, and eventually retired without disrupting the partners built on them
  • Strong judgment about data reliability at scale — you think in terms of what happens when a feed is late, incomplete, duplicated, or wrong, and you design for those cases deliberately
  • Experience working directly with external technical partners — you can hold a substantive conversation with a partner's engineering team and represent Lively's position credibly without an engineer in the room
  • Technical depth sufficient to be self-sufficient — you investigate data questions yourself rather than routing every one to engineering, and engineers regard your specifications as complete
  • Experience handling sensitive personal or financial data under a regulated framework, with an instinct for privacy, security, and auditability
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize complex data into clear product decisions
  • Outstanding communication skills — you can align engineers, partners, and executives on a shared direction
  • Strong familiarity with Agile methodologies and standard product tooling
  • Bachelor's degree in a technical or business field, or equivalent practical experience

What Sets You Apart

  • Benefits or health insurance domain experience — HSA/FSA/HRA plans, benefits compliance, IRS regulations, or the administration workflows behind them
  • Ecosystem familiarity with payroll providers, HR platforms, benefits administration systems, carriers, or third-party administrators
  • Fluency with industry data standards used in benefits, insurance, healthcare, or financial services exchange
  • Experience modernizing a legacy integration surface — migrating partners onto a new model without breaking the old one
  • Experience evaluating integration and connectivity vendors, and owning the build/buy/partner decision
  • Experience building AI-powered product experiences, including designing for reliability and user trust
  • Experience spanning both B2B (employer/broker-facing) and B2C (employee-facing) products
  • Leadership experience, including mentoring or developing junior PMs
  • Growth mindset and high self-motivation — you identify the next problem rather than waiting for it to be assigned

WHY LIVELY

Healthcare and financial benefits affect everyone — and most platforms in this space are still frustratingly hard to use. Lively exists to change that. You'll work on products that matter, with a team that cares about craft, velocity, and outcomes.

What you can expect:

  • A fast-paced, AI-augmented product environment where you'll work with cutting-edge tools daily
  • Meaningful ownership — this is not a role where you're handed a backlog and told to groom it
  • A collaborative, intellectually honest culture where good ideas win regardless of seniority
  • Direct impact on products used by thousands of employers and millions of employees
  • Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits (yes, we eat our own cooking), and remote-friendly flexibility
The base salary listed is a range for this position. Actual pay will depend on the candidate’s location and experience.
$165,000—$195,000 USD

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet all of the qualifications, but feel you would be a good fit for the position.

Benefits & Perks

We offer competitive salaries, stock options, medical, dental, vision, life and disability coverage. An HSA with employer contribution, FSA, paid parental leave, medical travel benefits, a 401k plan, flexible vacation policy, lifestyle spending accounts, and more!

At Lively, we believe having diverse teams in which everyone can be their authentic self is key to our success. We encourage people from underrepresented backgrounds to apply. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Come join us in our mission to help people optimize their healthcare spending, maximize their savings, and better their livelihood!

CaptivateIQ is transforming the way companies plan, manage, and optimize sales performance. Recognized by industry analysts like Forrester and G2 and backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia, ICONIQ, Accel, and Sapphire Ventures, we empower high-growth companies like Netflix, Figma, and Stripe with the flexibility and insights needed to drive revenue performance.

About the Role

The Modeling Platform team is the backbone of every product in CaptivateIQ's modeling suite and sits at the core of CaptivateIQ's multi-year product strategy. This team is a force multiplier — the components, interfaces, and infrastructure it builds are what let every product engineering team ship modeling experiences fast, without re-solving foundational problems each time.

The team's surface area spans service-layer APIs, a modeling SDK, and extensible frontend components — and our goal is to evolve this into a self-service framework: simple enough to ship new modeling products at a fraction of today's build time, reliable enough that product teams don't think about the plumbing, and opinionated enough that they aren't re-solving the same problems every iteration. We're also building this as an AI-native platform, with first-class access and support for AI agents to build alongside human engineers.

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to own the technical direction of that evolution — a technical leader with strong engineering chops who embodies CaptivateIQ's values of ownership, bias toward action, and delivering real impact. You'll set the architectural direction for how the platform evolves, drive the multi-year technical strategy (with your EM and senior EPD leadership as partners, not gatekeepers), and make the tradeoffs that determine how product teams build on top of it.

It's a highly collaborative role — you'll work daily with cross-functional partners (Product, Design, EM) and with the product engineering teams building on the platform. You'll also partner closely with the SmartGrid team — CaptivateIQ's proprietary DAG-based computation engine that powers the framework underneath — helping shape architectural direction for the Modeling Platform Pillar as a whole. You'll drive technical alignment across teams, and invest deeply in coaching and developing engineers toward senior and staff-level impact.

jobs.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer (Observability)
jobs.excerpt: introductionIAM Cloud builds software that simplifies IT management in the cloud.
jobs.description:
introduction

IAM Cloud builds software that simplifies IT management in the cloud. We are a fully employee owned, bootstrapped company - which means we answer to our customers and our team, not investors. With around 35 employees, we serve more than 3,000 organisations worldwide.

Being employee owned shapes how we work. Decisions are long-term, the culture is collaborative, and the people who build the company share in its success. We have leaned deliberately into AI and agentic workflows across the business as a core part of how a focused team competes with companies ten times our size. We are fully remote with employees in the UK, Ireland, Spain, Germany and Argentina and have been remote for years, as a deliberate choice about how good work gets done.

about the role

IAM Cloud is an Azure-first SaaS company with a small, fully remote engineering team. We run our own platform end to end: infrastructure, pipelines, releases and production operations all sit with the same handful of engineers. That means ownership is broad, documentation matters, and reducing toil is treated as a first-class goal rather than a side project.

We recently added a Senior Cloud Platform Engineer to own our CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code foundations. This role is the reliability counterpart: the person who owns how we see, measure and respond to what production is doing. You will own monitoring, observability, alerting and on-call at IAM Cloud, as the person who sets the standards, writes the policy and makes the engineering team better at running its own services.

Today our telemetry lives in Azure Monitor, Log Analytics and Application Insights, with Azure Managed Grafana for dashboards and alerting. It works, but it has grown organically. Alert thresholds are inherited rather than designed, retention and cost are not governed, instrumentation is inconsistent across services, and our on-call tooling is reaching end of life and must be replaced on a fixed deadline in the first half of 2027. We want someone who can come in, take a clear-eyed look at all of that, and turn it into something deliberate.

Where we are heading

Over the medium term we intend to move more of our workloads onto Kubernetes (AKS), with Prometheus alongside Azure Monitor and OpenTelemetry as the instrumentation standard. That is a direction rather than a dated plan, and it is not the focus of this role in its first year. What matters now is that whoever owns observability here has a view on what good looks like on that platform, so that the standards you set today carry over cleanly when we get there.

What you will own (outcomes)

  • Define and evolve the observability strategy, target architecture and standards for the platform - what we instrument, how, where it lands, how long we keep it and what it costs.
  • Make Grafana the place engineers go to understand production: dashboards and alerting designed around services and customer journeys, not around whichever metrics happened to be available.
  • Establish service level objectives for our customer-facing services, with error budgets that engineering and product actually use to make decisions.
  • Rationalise alerting so that every page is actionable, owned and has a runbook - and so that the on-call engineer's phone is quiet when nothing is wrong.
  • Lead and champion the move to a modern incident response and on-call platform (incident.io or similar) integrated with Microsoft Teams, and design the on-call model around it: rota, escalation, and the post-incident review process that feeds back into the backlog.
  • Champion observability-first thinking across the engineering team, so developers instrument their own services well without needing you in the loop.

First-quarter deliverables

  • A written telemetry governance policy covering Log Analytics table plans, retention tiers, sampling and cardinality controls - with a baseline of current ingestion and spend and a target.
  • An alert rationalisation pass across Azure Monitor and Grafana: every remaining alert mapped to a service, an owner, a severity and a runbook; noisy or unowned alerts removed or downgraded.
  • Selection, delivery and cutover of a new incident response and on-call platform (incident.io or similar, Teams-integrated) to replace our current tooling before its end-of-life date, including parallel running and a documented on-call model.
  • SLOs and SLIs defined for the top customer-facing services, with dashboards and burn-rate alerting.
  • Looking further out: as our Kubernetes and Prometheus direction firms up, you will own the observability standards for it - collector topology, log routing, dashboards and alerting - so that it lands well-instrumented from day one.

Day to day

  • Design and implement OpenTelemetry instrumentation across our .NET services, and the collector pipelines that shape, sample and route telemetry.
  • Own Azure Monitor, Log Analytics and Application Insights configuration, managed as code alongside the rest of our estate (Bicep first).
  • Own Grafana end to end: data sources, dashboards-as-code, alert rules and the conventions the team follows when adding to them.
  • Run the incident response and on-call platform once it is in place: routing, escalation policies, integrations with Azure Monitor and Grafana alerting, and the Teams workflow around an incident.
  • Contribute observability requirements and standards to our Kubernetes and Prometheus direction as it takes shape, alongside the platform engineer who owns that work.
  • Build and maintain Grafana dashboards and alert rules that answer real operational questions, and retire the ones that don't.
  • Lead incident response when it matters, run blameless post-incident reviews, and turn findings into engineering work.
  • Track and reduce reliability metrics that matter: MTTR, alert volume per on-call shift, incident recurrence, telemetry cost per service.
  • Evaluate tooling and AI-assisted operations capabilities on their merits, and give the team a clear recommendation rather than a shortlist.
  • Write things down: standards, runbooks, decision records, and the "why" behind thresholds.
  • Take part in a light-touch on-call rotation with the rest of the engineering team.

what we're looking for

What we're looking for (must-haves)

  • 6+ years in engineering, with 3+ in a reliability, observability or production-operations role where you owned outcomes rather than executed tickets.
  • You have defined SLOs, SLIs and error budgets for real services and can talk through how they changed decisions.
  • You have reduced alert noise - you can describe an alerting estate you inherited, what you cut, what you kept, and how you knew it was safe.
  • Hands-on OpenTelemetry: instrumenting services, running collectors, and making deliberate choices about sampling and cardinality.
  • Telemetry cost and retention governance: you understand that observability has a bill, and you have managed it.
  • Deep Azure Monitor / Log Analytics / Application Insights experience, including KQL, and strong Grafana skills - dashboards, alerting and managing both as code.
  • Infrastructure as code - Bicep is our standard; strong Terraform experience is fully transferable.
  • Clear written and spoken communication at C1 level or above, or native-level business English. You will be setting policy for a remote team; if it isn't written down, it doesn't exist.

Nice to have

  • Experience selecting, implementing or migrating incident-management and on-call platforms - strongly desirable given the first-quarter deliverables.
  • Prometheus-based monitoring and alerting, including exporters, recording rules and cardinality management.
  • Kubernetes in production, ideally AKS, and the observability patterns that go with it.
  • A software development background, ideally .NET, so instrumentation conversations with developers are peer to peer.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted operations and coding tools, and a considered view on where they help and where they don't.
  • Azure certifications (AZ-104, AZ-400, AZ-305) or the CKA.
  • Experience in a small or scale-up environment where you were the observability function.

why us?

How we work

  • Fully remote across the UK. We meet in person a few times a year for team events, but day-to-day work is remote.
  • Small, senior team. You will work directly with engineering leadership and have real input into technical decisions.
  • Async-friendly. We use writing as our default mode of communication and avoid meetings when a written update will do.
  • On-call is shared and light. We invest in making the platform boring rather than relying on heroics.

Our Offer
£80,000 - £95,000 salary (dependent on skills & experience)

Guaranteed £2,000 pay rise every year you're with us, separate from any merit or promotion increases.

Time off and flexibility

  • 26 days holiday plus public holidays, with the option to swap public holidays for days that are more meaningful to you.
  • Your birthday and work anniversary day off, every year.
  • Up to 4 weeks per year working from anywhere in the world.
  • Genuinely flexible, fully remote working - we trust you to manage your own time.

Health, family, and wellbeing – UK employees

  • Generous Becoming a Parent leave, designed to support every kind of family.
  • Medical scheme including remote GP, dental, optical, and diagnostics.
  • Access to Support Room - confidential counselling, therapy, and coaching.
  • Help@Hand employee assistance programme.
  • 5x salary life insurance through Unum.

Money and growth

  • Up to 10% pension match (UK employees).
  • Annual learning and development budget per function.

Interview process

We respect your time and aim to keep this efficient. Our typical process looks like this:
  • Initial conversation (45-60 minutes): a chat with our Head of People about you, the role, and any questions you have.
  • Technical conversation (60-90 minutes): a discussion with a couple of our senior engineers about your experience, our stack, and how you've approached real problems. This will also include a short, scoped live exercise relevant to the work you'd actually do here.
  • Final conversation (45-60 minutes): meet our CIO and one or two future team-mates to talk about the team, the company, and the road ahead.

Grey is a fast-growing company building the future of global banking for a borderless world. We provide multi-currency accounts, instant international transfers, and virtual cards that enable individuals and businesses to manage money across borders as easily as in their local currency. We serve digital nomads, remote workers, freelancers, international students, entrepreneurs, and anyone whose financial life crosses borders.

Licensed and regulated in multiple countries, Grey is expanding rapidly across global markets. We’re a remote company with staff around the world.

The opportunity

As our Senior Content Writer, you will be one of the most experienced writers on Grey's content team, producing our highest-quality editorial work while helping raise the standard of everything the team publishes. This is not a volume role. It’s a quality-first editorial role with real influence over how Grey tells stories.

You will write the pieces that define Grey's voice: thought leadership, brand storytelling, feature narratives, and editorially-led content that sets us apart from generic fintech copy. You will also co-own Grey's branded newsletter, develop content briefs that guide the wider writing team, and provide first-pass editorial review on other writers' drafts before they reach the Head of Content Strategy.

Grey is building a premium, editorially-led brand. We write like a publication, not a startup blog. If you care about craft, edit your own work before anyone asks, and can write something that feels expensive without trying too hard, this role will give you the platform and the audience to do your best work.

This is a full-time role. You will report to the Head of Content Strategy and work closely with the SEO manager, Product Marketing, Social Media, and Video teams.

What you'll do at Grey includes, but is not limited to:

  • Writing and editorial production
    • Deliver a steady cadence of high-impact editorial work, prioritizing strategic, editorially demanding pieces: thought leadership, brand storytelling, feature narratives, and long-form editorial.
    • Source and interview interesting people, especially freelancers, founders, remote workers, digital nomads, and members of Grey’s community.
    • Produce landing page copy, product launch content, and feature announcements as needed.
    • Write in Grey's editorial voice consistently: confident, clear, human, premium. No corporate filler. No generic fintech tone.
    • Self-edit rigorously. Your first drafts should require light editing, not rewriting.
    SEO content production
    • Write SEO-driven articles from detailed keyword briefs, including structured H2 outlines, word count targets per section, and secondary keyword placements
    • Produce comparison content, how-to guides, and listicles that target specific search queries while maintaining Grey's editorial voice
    • Write FAQ sections with answers that add substantive new information, structured for schema markup
    • Follow product accuracy and compliance requirements on all content (fee claims, product feature descriptions, and market-specific details require verification before publication).
    • Collaborate with the SEO manager on keyword research, content briefs, and search performance iteration
  • Newsletter ownership
    • Co-own The Gig Economy (Grey's branded newsletter) end-to-end: editorial planning, drafting, production, and send.
    • Develop the newsletter's editorial identity and grow its value to readers over time.
    • Identify stories from Grey’s blog, community, and wider conversations that can become engaging newsletter content.
    • Track newsletter performance and iterate on format, content mix, and tone based on data.
  • Editorial support and quality
    • Provide first-pass editorial review of contract writers' drafts before they go to the Head of Content Strategy. Flag quality issues, structural problems, and voice inconsistencies.
    • Contribute to editorial planning by surfacing story ideas, trends, people, and conversations Grey should be covering.
    • Help maintain and evolve Grey's editorial style guide and writing standards.
  • Content surfaces
    • Blog and long-form editorial, including SEO-driven articles and thought leadership.
    • Interviews, profiles, money diaries, reported features, first-person stories, data stories, and opinion pieces.
    • Product and feature content: launch announcements, landing pages, in-app copy.
    • Campaign copy as needed for major initiatives.
    • Event content and partner activations as assigned.
    • Grey Business (B2B) content: case studies and product narratives as needed.
  • Cross-functional collaboration
    • Work with the SEO manager to ensure content meets search intent and optimization requirements without compromising editorial quality.
    • Support the Social Media Lead and Video Marketing Lead with copy and narrative direction when needed.
    • Collaborate with Product Marketing on feature positioning and go-to-market content.
    • Work with community-facing teams to identify contributors, interview subjects, and stories from Grey’s user base.
    • Coordinate translation requirements for multilingual content.

Reporting structure

  • Reports to: CML

You’ll be a great fit if you meet these criteria:

  • 3+ years of professional writing experience in content marketing, editorial, journalism, or brand communications
  • A portfolio that shows range: you can write a compelling reported feature, profile, or interviewand a product landing page and a newsletter, and all three sound like the same brand wrote them.
  • Strong editorial judgment. You can spot what’s actually interesting in a topic, find the strongest angle, and know when a draft needs more reporting or development. This includes work, culture, travel, people, cities, careers, and lifestyle.
  • Experience writing for digital audiences with an understanding of how people read online
  • Experience writing long-form SEO content from keyword briefs, including structuring articles around search intent, writing to H2 keyword maps, and producing content formats like comparisons, listicles, and FAQ sections. You understand that SEO writing at Grey means writing for humans first while meeting specific structural and keyword requirements.
  • Comfortable working within strict product accuracy constraints. You’ll verify claims before publishing and follow compliance guidelines on how Grey's products are described across different markets.
  • You are reliable, organized, and deadline-driven. You deliver on time without being chased
  • Clear, direct communication. You ask questions early, flag blockers immediately, and don't disappear when things get hard
  • Experience reviewing or editing other writers' work is a strong plus
  • You read widely, and your writing reflects influences beyond fintech and SaaS content
  • Excellent written and verbal communication. You write clearly, concisely, and in a human voice. No corporate jargon
  • You are proactive, organized, and direct. You flag problems early, communicate honestly, and do not need to be micromanaged
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills with the ability to influence senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
  • Proven ability to work effectively in remote-first environments with distributed international teams

Nice to have:

  • Experience in fintech, financial services, or a regulated industry
  • Background in editorial, publishing, lifestyle brands, or culture-forward companies
  • Experience building or contributing to recurring editorial franchises/series
  • Experience writing B2B content (case studies, product pages, sales enablement)
  • Experience with email marketing and newsletter production
  • Familiarity with CMS platforms, content management workflows, and editorial tools
  • Understanding of digital nomad, remote work, and freelancer communities
  • Multilingual writing capabilities relevant to Grey's target markets

What’s in it for you:

  • None of us would go to work for free, so we ensure that your salary correctly compensates you for your time.
  • We become invested in your growth and provide you with access to a professional development budget for courses, conferences, certifications, and skill-enhancement opportunities.
  • When you need time away to re-group, we’ll make it happen and pay you for your time off.
  • Benefit from our great people culture and work alongside the most incredible team at Grey
  • Meet your wonderful teammates and relax at our yearly team offsite.

We want to hear from you if you're a writer who cares about craft, takes ownership of your work, and wants to shape the voice of a product used by people across 170+ countries. Join our team and help us build the future of borderless money.

jobs.description:
Our client is a Singapore-based fintech group with regional hubs in Lithuania and Dubai, and operations in Thailand, Indonesia, and the Philippines. Their operation is fully legal and compliant, with licenses in multiple countries and jurisdictions globally. Via their flagship product, they offer a cross-border payment solution infrastructure for money transfer operators, local banks, and corporates. With their mobile application, their retail customers and SMEs across Southeast Asia can send money to their families, friends, and business partners around the world.

﻿

Role Overview

We are seeking a highly experienced and results-oriented Senior Director of Sales to lead our client’s global sales strategy within the Money Transfer Operator (MTO) and Payment Service Provider (PSP) sectors. This critical leadership role will be responsible for driving significant revenue growth, managing their global sales team, and expanding their footprint into key international markets. The ideal candidate will possess a deep understanding of the MTO/PSP landscape, a proven track record of exceeding sales targets, and an extensive network within major banks, MTOs, and payment service providers.

Job Type: Full Time

Workplace: Remote

Requirements

  • Minimum of 10 years of progressive sales leadership experience, with a significant focus on the Money Transfer Operator (MTO) and/or Payment Service Provider (PSP) sectors.
  • Demonstrated experience with major banks, MTOs (e.g., Western Union, MoneyGram, Ria), and prominent payment service providers is essential.
  • Proven track record of consistently exceeding sales quotas and driving substantial revenue growth in complex, global environments.
  • Extensive and verifiable network of relationships with key decision-makers and influencers within the MTO and PSP industries.
  • Deep understanding of the global payments landscape, including regulatory frameworks, compliance requirements, and technological trends (e.g., real-time payments, blockchain, open banking).
  • Exceptional leadership and team management skills, with the ability to inspire, motivate, and develop a high-performing sales force across diverse geographies.
  • Strong strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent negotiation, communication (written and verbal), and presentation skills.
  • Ability to travel internationally as required.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, or a related field; MBA preferred.
  • Strongly Preferred: Have client list ready to integrate

Responsibilities

  • Strategic Sales Leadership: Develop, implement, and refine comprehensive global sales strategies for the MTO and PSP segments to achieve ambitious revenue targets and market share growth.
  • Revenue Management: Own the global MTO/PSP revenue pipeline, forecasting, and P&L. Implement effective pricing strategies and negotiate high-value contracts to maximize profitability.
  • Global Market Expansion: Identify and prioritize new market opportunities within the MTO and PSP ecosystems. Develop and execute go-to-market strategies for international expansion.
  • Team Leadership & Development: Recruit, mentor, and lead a high-performing global sales team. Foster a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement. Provide ongoing coaching, performance management, and career development opportunities.
  • Client Relationship Management: Cultivate and maintain strong, strategic relationships with key decision-makers within major banks, MTOs, and PSPs globally. Act as a trusted advisor and thought leader in the industry.
  • Partnership Development: Identify, evaluate, and forge strategic partnerships that accelerate market penetration and enhance our product/service offerings.
  • Market Intelligence: Stay abreast of industry trends, competitive landscape, regulatory changes, and technological advancements within the MTO and PSP space to inform sales strategies and product development.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with product, marketing, operations, and legal teams to ensure alignment of sales strategies with overall business objectives and to effectively bring new solutions to market.
  • Reporting & Analysis: Provide regular, insightful reports on sales performance, market trends, and pipeline status to senior leadership. Utilize data to drive informed decision-making.
